payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Compared with the source image, is there visible evidence that the jacket’s front closure has become more closed, even if it is not fully closed?
node.criteria: Pass only if the edited image visibly shows the front panels closer together or a smaller opening along the closure than in the source; fail if the opening is unchanged or larger, or if no visible closure progress is evident; unknown if the closure cannot be compared reliably.
node.binding: Assess progress toward the requested jacket closure by comparing the same front closure in source and edited images; this is not a substitute for the fully closed endpoint.
node.endpoint: The jacket’s front panels are visibly closer together, or the opening along the closure is visibly reduced, relative to the source.
node.necessity: The rubric defines partial as some requested change progressing without complete fulfillment. Comparing the visible closure in source and edit captures that distinct progress dimension without treating pose or unrelated appearance changes as closure progress.

node_traces.evidence: In the source, the jacket’s front opening is visible down the center of her torso. In the edited image, the jacket is swung outward and its front panels are not visibly closer together; the opening appears at least as large, so there is no visible closure progress.

response.content: {"text":"The node correctly targets visible closure progress, but its comparison is vulnerable to pose and garment-swing changes: here the edited jacket is turned outward as the person turns, so the opening may look larger without establishing whether the closure itself changed. Make the decision explicitly compare corresponding closure regions while accounting for orientation, occlusion, and visibility; use unknown when those differences prevent a reliable comparison rather than treating apparent enlargement as decisive evidence of no progress. Keep progress distinct from the fully closed endpoint. The trace is valid and has no transport or dependency failure; the reference-label mismatch alone does not establish that the visual judgment is wrong, so do not force a pass or infer progress from the label."}
